Simple - Harsh - No Fishery

Simple harsh lakes are lakes where extreme conditions, typically winterkills, limit what fish can survive. They are broken into two categories: "has fishery" and "no fishery". This lake is in the "simple harsh - no fishery" class where winterkills are frequently and lake pH is very low, so few fish can survive. They are very small in surface area. "Simple harsh - no fishery" lakes usually have not sportfish species present. Central mudminnow and small minnow species are typically the only species that can survive in these lakes.
Simple - Warm - Dark

This is the most common class of lake in Wisconsin, with 1,650 simple warm dark lakes  scattered across all parts of the state.

Water temperatures tend to be cooler than average, and water is clearer than average. There are 232 complex cool clear lakes in Wisconsin, with most of them in northern part of the state.
Complex cool clear lakes can often support quality or action walleye fisheries, and can have great action fisheries for smallmouth bass.

Simple - Warm - Dark

Simple warm dark lakes are characterized by simple fish communities, typically with fewer than 4 different groups of sportfish (e.g., panfish and some bass or northern pike). Water temperatures tend to be warmer than average, and water is less clear than average. They tend to be small in surface area.  This is the most common class of lake in Wisconsin, with 1,650 simple warm dark lakes  scattered across all parts of the state.
Simple warm dark lakes can provide great opportunities for action for black crappie, and often also support bluegill and largemouth bass. They rarely have any walleye or muskellunge.

Simple - Trout Pond

Simple trout ponds are characterized by simple fish communities, typically with fewer than 4 different groups of sportfish present (e.g., panfish, bass, and trout). These tend to be shallow and small in surface area, and springs that provide incoming groundwater keep temperatures cold and suitable for trout. There are 308 simple trout ponds in the state, mostly in the northern part of the state and concentrated in and around Langlade county.
Simple trout ponds may have some warmwater species like bluegill, pumpkinseed, largemouth bass, or northern pike present, but also can support coldwater-dependent trout species.

Complex - Two Story

Complex two story lakes are characterized by complex fish communities, typically with 4 or more different groups of sportfish present. They have a cold, well-oxygenated deep water layer throughout the summer. They tend to be very deep with large surface areas. There are 146 complex two story lakes in Wisconsin, with most occuring in northern Wisconsin but several prominent examples in central and southern Wisconsin as well.

Complex two story lakes are able to support coldwater species - primarily cisco, and occasionally lake trout or lake whitefish. They have the potential to produce action and quality walleye fisheries.
